record.context_brief: Increasing-label paths in edge-labeled complete graphs.
record.original_question: Label the edges of the complete graph K_n bijectively by 1, 2, ..., binom(n, 2). For a labeling lambda, let l(lambda) be the length of the longest simple path whose edge labels strictly increase along the path, and let f(n) be the minimum of l(lambda) over all such labelings. Determine the growth of f(n), in particular whether f(n) = o(n) and whether f(n) > n^(1/2 + epsilon) for some epsilon > 0.

evidence.quote: Is f(n) = o(n)? Is f(n) > n^(1/2)+e for some e > 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer n ≥ 2, consider all bijective labelings λ : E(K_n) → {1, 2, …, C(n,2)} of the edges of the complete graph on n vertices. For such a labeling λ, let ℓ(λ) be the length (number of edges) of the longest simple path v_0 v_1 … v_k in K_n whose edge labels are strictly increasing, i.e. λ(v_0 v_1) < λ(v_1 v_2) < … < λ(v_{k-1} v_k). Define
   f(n) = min_λ ℓ(λ),
the minimum being taken over all bijective edge-labelings of K_n.

Determine the asymptotic growth rate of f(n). In particular:
(a) Is f(n) = o(n)?
(b) Does there exist ε > 0 such that f(n) > n^{1/2 + ε} for all sufficiently large n?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem (originally posed by Chvátal and Komlós, 1971) is partially solved. Bucić, Kwan, Pokrovskiy, Sudakov, Tran, and Wagner (2018/2020, "Nearly-linear monotone paths in edge-ordered graphs", Israel J. Math.) proved f(n) ≥ n^{1-o(1)}, which in particular answers (b) affirmatively for every ε < 1/2. The original conjecture that f(n) is linear in n, and the question whether f(n) = o(n), remain open.

status_evidence.title: Nearly-linear monotone paths in edge-ordered graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Any edge-ordering of the complete graph contains a monotone path of length n^{1-o(1)}, almost closing the gap to the conjectured linear bound.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bound f(n) ≥ n^{1-o(1)} is established, settling whether f(n) > n^{1/2+ε}, but the question whether f(n) = o(n) remains open.

status_evidence.title: Increasing paths in edge ordered graphs (1971)
status_evidence.snippet: Chvátal and Komlós asked in 1971 to determine f(K_n), the largest k such that every edge-ordering contains an increasing path of length k.
status_evidence.claim: The problem originates with Chvátal and Komlós (1971) and the exact growth rate of f(n) is not yet determined.
